description: How a 3D model is looked at and presented: UCS management, ViewCube, SteeringWheels and navigation bar, named views and ShowMotion shots, cameras, walk/fly and motion-path animation, the legacy DVIEW/HIDE/SHADEMODE commands, the Visual Styles Manager, the render window, presets, environment and exposure, materials and lights, and the Model Documentation commands (VIEWBASE and its projected, section and detail views) plus 3D print, STL, 3D DWF and the CAD-format import/export commands.

tools.name: UCSMAN
tools.description: Opens the UCS dialog with three tabs: Named UCSs (list of saved coordinate systems with Set Current and Details, including World and Previous), Orthographic UCSs (Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right relative to World or a named UCS, with a depth value) and Settings (UCS icon on/off, display at origin, allow selecting the icon; save UCS with viewport, update view to Plan when UCS changes). It is the dialog counterpart of the UCS command's Named/Save/Restore options.
tools.usage:
UCSMAN  (alias UC; View tab > Coordinates > dialog launcher)
UCS N S name      (command-line save)
UCS N R name      (command-line restore)

parameters.name: Named UCSs tab
parameters.description: Double-click to set current; right-click to rename or delete; Details shows origin and axis vectors.

parameters.name: Orthographic UCSs tab
parameters.description: Six standard orientations relative to a base UCS, with Depth to offset the plane.

parameters.name: Settings tab
parameters.description: UCSICON display options and the UCSVIEW / UCSFOLLOW behaviours.

parameters.name: UCSVP
parameters.description: Per-viewport variable: 1 locks the UCS to the viewport, 0 follows the current UCS.

tools.example:
UCS 3 (define a UCS on the sloped face)
UCSMAN (Named UCSs: rename 'Unnamed' to ROOF-SLOPE)
...
UCS N R ROOF-SLOPE
PLAN C
tools.notes: Named UCSs are stored in the UCS symbol table and can be purged. In model documentation and dynamic UCS (UCSDETECT) workflows named UCSs are less needed, but they remain the reliable way to script repeatable working planes.

tools.name: NAVVCUBE
tools.description: Turns the ViewCube on or off and opens its settings: the ViewCube is the clickable cube in the corner of the drawing area whose faces, edges and corners set standard and isometric views, whose ring rotates the view, and whose compass and WCS/UCS menu switch between coordinate systems and parallel/perspective projection. NAVVCUBEDISPLAY, NAVVCUBELOCATION, NAVVCUBEOPACITY, NAVVCUBESIZE and NAVVCUBEORIENT store the settings.
tools.usage:
NAVVCUBE
Enter an option [ON/OFF/Settings] <ON>:
Settings: ViewCube Settings dialog - on-screen position, size, inactive opacity, show UCS menu, snap to closest view, zoom to extents after view change, use view transitions, orient to current UCS, keep scene upright, show compass

parameters.name: NAVVCUBEDISPLAY
parameters.description: 0 off, 1 on in 3D visual styles, 2 on in 2D wireframe, 3 on in both (default 3).

parameters.name: NAVVCUBELOCATION / SIZE / OPACITY
parameters.description: Corner (0-3), size (0 automatic, 1 tiny .. 4 large), inactive opacity 0-100.

parameters.name: NAVVCUBEORIENT
parameters.description: 0 orient to WCS, 1 to the current UCS.

parameters.name: Home view
parameters.description: Right-click the cube > Set Current View as Home; the house icon returns to it.

tools.example:
NAVVCUBE
S
(untick 'Zoom to extents after view change', OK)
; script: hide it while plotting previews
NAVVCUBEDISPLAY 0
tools.notes: The cube is only visible in the current viewport. Clicking a face while in a 3D visual style keeps perspective if PERSPECTIVE is 1; in 2D wireframe it forces parallel projection. Not shown in the Core Console.

tools.name: NAVSWHEEL
tools.description: Displays a SteeringWheel, a cursor-tracking menu of navigation tools: the 2D wheel (Pan, Zoom, Rewind), the View Object wheel (Center, Zoom, Rewind, Orbit), the Tour Building wheel (Forward, Look, Rewind, Up/Down) and the Full Navigation wheel combining all eight tools plus Walk, with mini versions of each. Rewind replays the view history as thumbnails. NAVSWHEELMODE, NAVSWHEELOPACITY, NAVSWHEELSIZE and the walk speed live in the wheel's settings dialog.
tools.usage:
NAVSWHEEL  (Shift+W; navigation bar > wheel button)
(right-click the wheel: choose wheel type, Go Home, Fit to Window, Restore Original Center, Level Camera, Increase/Decrease Walk Speed, SteeringWheel Settings..., Close Wheel)

parameters.name: NAVSWHEELMODE
parameters.description: 0 big View Object, 1 big Tour Building, 2 big Full Navigation, 3 mini View Object, 4 mini Tour Building, 5 mini Full Navigation, 6 2D wheel.

parameters.name: Center tool
parameters.description: Sets the pivot for Orbit/Zoom by clicking a point on the model.

parameters.name: Walk / Up-Down
parameters.description: First-person movement, height slider - the same engine as 3DWALK.

tools.example:
NAVSWHEELMODE 2
NAVSWHEEL
(hold Orbit and drag; release; hold Rewind and slide back through previous views; Esc)
tools.notes: Esc or the X closes the wheel. Wheels work in 2D and 3D, but Orbit/Walk tools are unavailable in the Model tab when the visual style is 2D Wireframe and the view is plan in some releases.

tools.name: NAVBAR
tools.description: Shows or hides the navigation bar, the vertical strip next to the ViewCube holding SteeringWheels, Pan, Zoom (with flyout for extents/window/previous/realtime...), Orbit (flyout for orbit/free orbit/continuous) and ShowMotion buttons. NAVBARDISPLAY is the underlying variable; its position and docking follow the ViewCube.
tools.usage:
NAVBAR
Enter an option [ON/OFF] <ON>:
NAVBARDISPLAY = 0 | 1

parameters.name: customize menu
parameters.description: The small arrow at the bottom of the bar toggles which tools are shown and links the bar to the ViewCube position.

tools.example:
; minimal screen for a CAD manager profile
NAVBARDISPLAY 0
NAVVCUBEDISPLAY 0
tools.notes: The bar is per-drawing-window setting saved in the profile. In AutoCAD LT the Orbit tools are limited to 2D wireframe/3D orbit view-only.

tools.name: SHOWMOTION
tools.description: Opens the ShowMotion strip at the bottom of the drawing area showing thumbnails of the drawing's named views grouped by category, each optionally animated as a 'shot' (still, cinematic camera movement or recorded walk), and lets you play them in sequence for presentations. NAVSMOTION is the underlying command name, NAVSMOTIONCLOSE closes it, NEWSHOT creates a new animated view and VIEWPLAY plays one by name.
tools.usage:
SHOWMOTION  (alias NAVSMOTION; navigation bar > ShowMotion)
(strip: category thumbnails, Play All, Pin, New Shot, Close)
NAVSMOTIONCLOSE

parameters.name: Play All
parameters.description: Plays every shot in the current category in order with its transitions.

parameters.name: Loop / Pin
parameters.description: Keep the strip open and looping.

parameters.name: Category
parameters.description: Named views carry a category string (set in NEWVIEW/NEWSHOT) used to group thumbnails.

tools.example:
NEWSHOT (name Lobby, category Tour, Cinematic, Orbit 10 s)
NEWSHOT (name Atrium, category Tour, Zoom in 5 s)
SHOWMOTION
(click Tour > Play All)
tools.notes: Shots are stored with the named views in the drawing (VIEW command lists them). Playback uses the current visual style; recorded walks require 3DWALK to have been recorded into the shot.

tools.name: NEWSHOT
tools.description: Creates a named view with ShowMotion animation properties through the New View / Shot Properties dialog: a name and category, the view type (Cinematic with a movement such as Zoom In/Out, Track Left/Right, Crane Up/Down, Look, Orbit and their duration/distance; Still with a fade-in duration; Recorded Walk to capture a 3DWALK path), and the transition type between shots. NEWVIEW (2018.1) is the same dialog without the shot properties, saving a plain named view from the current display or a window.
tools.usage:
NEWSHOT
(New View / Shot Properties dialog: View name, View category, View type [Cinematic/Still/Recorded Walk]; View Properties tab: boundary current display / define window, settings to save with view (UCS, live section, visual style), background; Shot Properties tab: Transition type and duration, Movement type, duration, distance/degrees, playback preview)
NEWVIEW
(same dialog, View Properties only)

parameters.name: Cinematic movements
parameters.description: Zoom In, Zoom Out, Track Left, Track Right, Crane Up, Crane Down, Look, Orbit, with Duration and a distance/angle; Starting point / Half-way / Ending point option for where the current view sits in the move.

parameters.name: Transition
parameters.description: Fade from black / Fade from white / Cut to shot, with duration.

parameters.name: Recorded Walk
parameters.description: Press Start recording, navigate with 3DWALK keys, stop; the path replays.

tools.example:
NEWSHOT
(Name: Entrance; Category: Tour; Cinematic; Movement: Orbit, 8 seconds, 45 degrees; Transition: Fade from black 1 s; OK)
tools.notes: VIEW > New opens the same dialog. Shots do not export to video - use ANIPATH for AVI/MOV output or screen capture of ShowMotion playback.

tools.name: VIEWGO
tools.description: Restores a named view by name from the command line without the VIEW dialog, and VIEWPLAY plays the ShowMotion shot recorded with a named view. Both are what scripts and CUI macros use to jump to saved views (VIEWGO) or run a presentation shot (VIEWPLAY); -VIEW R name is the older equivalent of VIEWGO.
tools.usage:
VIEWGO
Enter view name: <name>
VIEWPLAY
Enter view name: <name>   (plays the shot's transition and movement)

parameters.name: view name
parameters.description: Any named view in the drawing (case-insensitive); model space views restore the UCS, layer state and visual style saved with them if those options were chosen.

tools.example:
; CUI macro on a button
^C^C_VIEWGO;NORTH-ELEVATION

; script
VIEWGO
SITE-OVERVIEW
-PLOT ...
tools.notes: A view saved with a layer snapshot restores layer visibility, which surprises users editing after VIEWGO - check the view's 'Restore layers' setting in the VIEW dialog. VIEWPLAY needs a shot; plain views just cut.

tools.name: DVIEW
tools.description: The legacy dynamic-view command that sets camera and target points, distance (which turns on perspective projection), pan, zoom (lens length in perspective), twist, and front/back clipping planes, previewing on a selected subset of objects or the DVIEWBLOCK house. Superseded by 3DORBIT, CAMERA and the ViewCube, it is still the only way to set an exact perspective by numbers in a script and to set a view twist angle.
tools.usage:
DVIEW
Select objects or <use DVIEWBLOCK>: <selection> Enter
Enter option [CAmera/TArget/Distance/POints/PAn/Zoom/TWist/CLip/Hide/Off/Undo]: <keyword>
CAmera: angle from XY plane, angle in XY plane from X axis
Distance: turns perspective on at the given camera-target distance
TWist: view twist angle
CLip: Back/Front/Off clipping distances
Off: turn perspective off

parameters.name: POints
parameters.description: Set target then camera point by coordinates - the deterministic way to define a view.

parameters.name: Zoom
parameters.description: Lens length (mm) in perspective; scale factor in parallel projection.

parameters.name: TWist
parameters.description: Rotate the view about the line of sight (sets VIEWTWIST); used for rotated plans without changing the UCS.

parameters.name: DVIEWBLOCK
parameters.description: A block named DVIEWBLOCK in the drawing replaces the default house preview.

tools.example:
; rotate the plan view 30 degrees on screen for a skewed site
DVIEW

TW
30

; scripted perspective
DVIEW (select) PO 0,0,0 50,-50,30 D 80 X
tools.notes: Perspective views set with DVIEW behave like CAMERA views (PERSPECTIVE 1); ZOOM/PAN are limited there. Objects edited while in a DVIEW twist keep world coordinates - only the display is rotated.

tools.name: 3DCLIP
tools.description: Opens the Adjust Clipping Planes window for the current 3D view, where front and back clipping planes are dragged to cut away geometry between the viewer and the model or behind it (a display-only cut, unlike LIVESECTION). Clipping is saved with named views and used to look inside buildings and mechanisms without sectioning.
tools.usage:
3DCLIP
(Adjust Clipping Planes window: Adjust Front Clipping, Adjust Back Clipping, Create Slice (move both together), Front Clipping On/Off, Back Clipping On/Off; drag the lines over the side view of the model)

parameters.name: FRONTZ / BACKZ
parameters.description: Read-only distances of the clipping planes from the target; VIEWMODE bits report whether they are on.

parameters.name: Create Slice
parameters.description: Locks the two planes at a fixed spacing so a thin slab can be swept through the model.

tools.example:
3DORBIT (set an interior viewpoint) Esc
3DCLIP
(click Front Clipping On, drag the front plane until the near wall disappears; close the window)
tools.notes: Clipping applies to the current viewport and is also reachable from the 3DORBIT shortcut menu > Adjust Clipping Planes. Plots of the viewport honour the clip. DVIEW's CLip option sets the same planes numerically.

tools.name: CAMERA
tools.description: Places a camera object (a glyph in model space) with a location, target, lens length, field of view and optional front/back clipping, and creates a matching named view. Selecting the camera shows its frustum with grips and a Camera Preview window; its properties (Name, Lens length, Field of view, Roll angle, Clipping) can be changed in Properties, and double-clicking sets the view. Cameras drive ANIPATH animations and perspective renderings.
tools.usage:
CAMERA
Current camera settings: Height=0  Lens Length=50 mm
Specify camera location: <point>
Specify target location: <point>
Enter an option [?/Name/LOcation/Height/Target/LEns/Clipping/View/eXit] <eXit>:

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Camera and view name (default Camera1...).

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: Z of the camera; CAMERAHEIGHT stores the default.

parameters.name: LEns
parameters.description: Focal length in mm (35 mm equivalent); shorter = wider field of view.

parameters.name: Clipping
parameters.description: Front/back clipping planes for the camera view.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: Switch to the camera's view immediately.

parameters.name: CAMERADISPLAY
parameters.description: 0 hides camera glyphs, 1 shows them.

tools.example:
CAMERA
1000,-2000,1600
1000,500,1200
N
ENTRANCE
LE
28
V
Y
X
tools.notes: Camera views are perspective; PERSPECTIVE and PERSPECTIVECLIP govern behaviour. Cameras appear in the VIEW dialog under Model Views and in ShowMotion; they plot as nothing but show in wireframe unless CAMERADISPLAY is 0.

tools.name: 3DWALK
tools.description: Walks through a 3D model in first person: the view moves with the W/A/S/D or arrow keys at a fixed eye height while the mouse turns the view, and a Position Locator window shows a plan of the model with the camera indicator. 3DFLY is the same without the height constraint (free flight). WALKFLYSETTINGS sets step size, steps per second and whether the instruction and locator windows appear; Shift-drag looks around, and the walk can be recorded into a ShowMotion shot.
tools.usage:
3DWALK  (alias 3DW)   /   3DFLY
(keys: W/Up forward, S/Down back, A/Left left, D/Right right; drag to look; Shift+drag to pan; Esc or Enter to exit)
WALKFLYSETTINGS
(Walk and Fly Settings dialog: display instruction window [when entering walk/fly mode / once per session / never], display Position Locator window; Current drawing settings: Walk/fly step size, Steps per second)

parameters.name: STEPSIZE
parameters.description: Distance per step in drawing units (default 6).

parameters.name: STEPSPERSEC
parameters.description: Steps per second when a key is held (default 2).

parameters.name: Position Locator
parameters.description: Palette with a top view; drag the camera or target indicators to relocate; shows preview toggle.

tools.example:
WALKFLYSETTINGS (step size 500 mm, 4 steps per second)
VSCURRENT C
3DWALK
(hold W to walk down the corridor, drag to look into rooms, Esc)
tools.notes: Requires a perspective view; 3DWALK switches to perspective automatically. Realistic and Conceptual visual styles with hardware acceleration give usable frame rates; large drawings may need a lower level of detail or frozen layers.

tools.name: ANIPATH
tools.description: Motion Path Animation: renders an animation to an AVI, MOV, MPG or WMV file by moving a camera along a path (polyline, line, arc, spline, circle) or a fixed point, with the target on another path, a point or none, at a chosen frame rate, frame count or duration, resolution and visual style (or render preset). It is AutoCAD's built-in fly-through generator for design review videos.
tools.usage:
ANIPATH
(Motion Path Animation dialog: Camera - Link camera to Point or Path; Target - Link target to Point, Path or None; Animation settings - Frame rate, Number of frames, Duration, Visual style, Format [AVI/MOV/MPG/WMV], Resolution, Corner deceleration, Reverse; Preview...; OK -> Save As dialog)

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Select an existing curve; the camera or target moves along it in the curve's direction (Reverse flips).

parameters.name: Corner deceleration
parameters.description: Slows the camera at sharp path corners.

parameters.name: Visual style
parameters.description: Any visual style, or a render preset for a rendered (slow) animation.

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: From 160x120 up to 1024x768 in the dialog list.

tools.example:
SPLINE (draw the camera route at eye height)
ANIPATH
(Camera: Path > pick the spline; Target: Point > click the building centre; 25 fps, 250 frames, Conceptual, WMV, 1024x768; Preview; OK; save tour.wmv)
tools.notes: Rendering with a render preset takes minutes per frame; preview with a visual style first. The path is stored as a named camera motion path in the drawing. Output codecs depend on Windows.

tools.name: VISUALSTYLES
tools.description: Opens the Visual Styles Manager palette listing the built-in visual styles - 2D Wireframe, Conceptual, Hidden, Realistic, Shaded, Shaded with edges, Shades of Gray, Sketchy, Wireframe, X-ray - and any custom ones, with a property grid to create or edit a style: face settings (face style Realistic/Gooch/None, lighting quality, colour mode, opacity, material display), environment settings (shadows, backgrounds), edge settings (mode Facet edges/Isolines/None, colour, occluded and intersection edges, silhouette edges width, edge modifiers line extensions and jitter for the hand-drawn look). VISUALSTYLESCLOSE closes it; VSCURRENT applies a style.
tools.usage:
VISUALSTYLES  (View tab > Visual Styles > dialog launcher; alias VSM)
(palette: Available Visual Styles thumbnails - Create New, Apply to Current Viewport, Export to Tool Palette, Delete; property grid for the selected style)
VISUALSTYLESCLOSE
-VISUALSTYLES  Enter an option [set Current/Saveas/Delete/?]

parameters.name: Face settings
parameters.description: VSFACESTYLE, VSLIGHTINGQUALITY, VSFACECOLORMODE, VSFACEOPACITY, VSMONOCOLOR, VSMATERIALMODE.

parameters.name: Environment settings
parameters.description: VSSHADOWS (0 none, 1 ground, 2 full), VSBACKGROUNDS.

parameters.name: Edge settings
parameters.description: VSEDGES (0 none, 1 isolines, 2 facet edges), VSEDGECOLOR, VSSILHEDGES / VSSILHWIDTH, VSOCCLUDEDEDGES / VSOCCLUDEDCOLOR / VSOCCLUDEDLTYPE, VSINTERSECTIONEDGES, VSEDGEJITTER, VSEDGEOVERHANG, VSHALOGAP, VSISOONTOP.

parameters.name: FASTSHADEDMODE
parameters.description: 2023+: cross-platform GPU graphics for shaded styles (0 off, 1 on); in 2026 also covers Hidden and Conceptual.

tools.example:
VISUALSTYLES
(Create New: 'PRESENTATION' from Shaded with edges; Face style Realistic; Lighting quality Smooth; Shadows Full; Silhouette edges On width 3; Apply to Current Viewport)
-VISUALSTYLES C PRESENTATION
tools.notes: Visual styles are saved in the drawing (purgeable) and can be dragged to a tool palette for reuse. Plotting a viewport with a shaded style uses the viewport's Shade plot property (As Displayed, Wireframe, Hidden, Rendered...).

tools.name: HIDE
tools.description: Regenerates the current view with hidden lines removed in the 2D Wireframe visual style, showing solids, surfaces, meshes, 3D faces, wide polylines and objects with thickness as opaque - a quick check of a 3D model without switching visual styles. Text can be hidden by geometry (HIDETEXT), obscured lines shown in a colour/linetype (OBSCUREDCOLOR, OBSCUREDLTYPE) and the accuracy set by HIDEPRECISION. The Hidden visual style is the modern, persistent equivalent.
tools.usage:
HIDE  (alias HI)  - no prompts; the hidden view lasts until the next REGEN/zoom in some releases or until the display refreshes
HIDETEXT = 0 text is not hidden nor hides | 1 (default) text is treated as an object
OBSCUREDLTYPE = 0 off, 1 solid, 2 dashed, 3 dotted ... 11 | OBSCUREDCOLOR = ACI
HIDEPRECISION = 0 single precision | 1 double precision (slower, more accurate)

parameters.name: DISPSILH
parameters.description: 1 removes the tessellation lines of curved solids in the hidden view, showing only silhouettes.

parameters.name: Viewport Shade plot = Hidden
parameters.description: The plotting equivalent for layouts (MVIEW > Shadeplot > Hidden).

tools.example:
VSCURRENT 2
DISPSILH 1
HIDE

; show hidden edges dashed instead of removing them
OBSCUREDLTYPE 2
OBSCUREDCOLOR 8
HIDE
tools.notes: HIDE does nothing in shaded visual styles. Objects on frozen layers are ignored but objects on turned-off layers still hide others (unlike frozen). In scripts, prefer the Hidden visual style since HIDE is transient.

tools.name: SHADEMODE
tools.description: Sets the visual style of the current viewport from the command line with the same options as VSCURRENT (2dwireframe, Wireframe, Hidden, Realistic, Conceptual, Shaded, shaded with Edges, shades of Gray, SKetchy, X-ray, Other for named styles). -SHADEMODE keeps the pre-2007 options (2D wireframe, 3D wireframe, Hidden, Flat, Gouraud, Flat+edges, Gouraud+edges) for old scripts, mapping them onto today's styles.
tools.usage:
SHADEMODE
Enter an option [2dwireframe/Wireframe/Hidden/Realistic/Conceptual/Shaded/shaded with Edges/shades of Gray/SKetchy/X-ray/Other] <current>:
-SHADEMODE
Enter option [2D wireframe/3D wireframe/Hidden/Flat/Gouraud/fLat+edges/gOuraud+edges] <current>:

parameters.name: Other
parameters.description: Type the name of a custom visual style.

parameters.name: legacy Flat / Gouraud
parameters.description: Map to Shaded / Realistic-like styles; kept for compatibility only.

tools.example:
; old script line still works
-SHADEMODE
H
; modern equivalent
SHADEMODE
H
tools.notes: Both write the viewport's visual style property; VSCURRENT is the documented command. SHADEDGE/SHADEDIF only affect the legacy SHADE command's output.

tools.name: RENDERWINDOW
tools.description: Displays the Render window (RENDERWIN alias) without starting a render: the window holds the render output area with zoom/pan, the render history list (each render with its size, time and preset), Save/Save Copy for the image (BMP, PNG, TIF, JPG, PCX, TGA) and, since 2016, the render size and preset drop-downs and the Render button itself. RENDER starts rendering into it; RENDERWINDOWCLOSE closes it; RENDERCROP renders a picked region of the viewport.
tools.usage:
RENDERWINDOW  (alias RENDERWIN)
RENDER  (renders the current view with the current preset into the window; -RENDER for scripts: preset, destination Window/Viewport/file, output size, file name)
RENDERCROP  Pick crop window to render: <two corners>
RENDERWINDOWCLOSE

parameters.name: Render Size
parameters.description: Preset sizes (e.g. 800 x 600 px SVGA) or More Output Settings for custom width/height/DPI and image size in inches/mm.

parameters.name: Render in
parameters.description: Window, Viewport or Region.

parameters.name: History
parameters.description: Right-click a row: Save, Make Render Settings Current, Remove from the list, Zoom to Fit.

parameters.name: -RENDER
parameters.description: Command-line render used in scripts: Enter render preset, Render destination [Viewport/Window/File], output file name and size.

tools.example:
-RENDER
High
F
1600
1200
C:/out/lobby.png

; or interactively
RENDERWINDOW (choose 1920 x 1080 px, preset Medium, click Render; Save)
tools.notes: Rendering needs a 3D view with materials and lights (or default lighting) and is unavailable in AutoCAD LT and the Core Console. Since 2016 the renderer is the Autodesk Raytracer (ART); mental ray settings from older drawings are ignored. Cloud rendering (RENDERONLINE) has been discontinued.

tools.name: RENDERPRESETS
tools.description: Opens the Render Presets Manager palette (2016+ layout) to choose and edit render presets: the standard Low, Medium, High, Coffee-Break Quality, Lunch Quality and Overnight Quality presets differ in render duration - by number of levels (iterations) or by time - and in lighting/material accuracy (Low, Draft, High). Custom presets are created as copies and become the current preset used by RENDER. RENDERPRESETSCLOSE closes the palette.
tools.usage:
RENDERPRESETS  (alias RPREF)
(Render Presets Manager: Current preset list; Create Copy, Delete; Preset Info name/description; Render Duration: Until Satisfactory / Render By Level (1-50) / Render By Time (minutes); Lights and Materials: Low / Draft / High)
RENDERPRESETSCLOSE

parameters.name: RENDERTARGET
parameters.description: 0 until satisfactory, 1 render by level, 2 render by time.

parameters.name: RENDERLEVEL / RENDERTIME
parameters.description: Iterations (1-50) or minutes for the render engine.

parameters.name: RENDERLIGHTCALC
parameters.description: 1 Low (simplified), 2 Draft (basic global illumination), 3 High (advanced GI, slow).

parameters.name: Render presets in the drawing
parameters.description: Presets are stored with the drawing and appear in the Render window drop-down.

tools.example:
RENDERPRESETS
(select High, Create Copy 'FINAL-4K', Render By Level 30, Lights and Materials High; close)
RENDERWINDOW (size 3840 x 2160, preset FINAL-4K, Render)
tools.notes: Higher levels reduce noise progressively; the render can be stopped early and saved. Pre-2016 presets (mental ray sampling, ray tracing depth) are not shown.

tools.name: RENDERENVIRONMENT
tools.description: Opens the Render Environment & Exposure palette (RENDEREXPOSURE opens the same palette to the exposure section since 2016): Environment turns image-based lighting on and picks an IBL image map (Sharp Highlights, Rim Lights, Grid Light, Snowy Field, Plaza, Dry Lake Bed... or a custom background) with rotation and the option to use it as a visible background; Exposure sets the exposure value (EXPVALUE, brightness) and white balance in Kelvin (EXPWHITEBALANCE). RENDERENVIRONMENTCLOSE / RENDEREXPOSURECLOSE close it.
tools.usage:
RENDERENVIRONMENT  or  RENDEREXPOSURE
(palette: Environment On/Off, Image Based Lighting map, Rotation, Use IBL Image as Background, Use Custom Background; Exposure value, White balance)
RENDERENVIRONMENTCLOSE

parameters.name: IBLENVIRONMENT
parameters.description: System variable naming the current image-based lighting map (0 = off).

parameters.name: EXPVALUE
parameters.description: Exposure (-21..21, default 8.6); lower = brighter.

parameters.name: EXPWHITEBALANCE
parameters.description: Colour temperature 1500-20000 K (default 6500).

parameters.name: RENDERENVSTATE
parameters.description: Reports whether the palette is open.

tools.example:
RENDERENVIRONMENT
(Environment On; Image Based Lighting: Plaza; Rotation 45; Use IBL Image as Background: On; Exposure 9.5; White balance 5500)
RENDER
tools.notes: IBL images supply both light and reflections; combine with SUNPROPERTIES for exterior daylight. Pre-2016 fog/depth-cue settings of the old Render Environment dialog no longer exist.

tools.name: MATERIALATTACH
tools.description: Opens the Material Attachment Options dialog to attach materials to layers by dragging a material from the drawing's material list onto a layer, so every object with Material = ByLayer on that layer renders with it. It is the fastest way to materialise a model that is organised by layer (walls, glass, floor). MATERIALMAP then adjusts how a texture is projected onto individual objects, and MATERIALASSIGN drags a material from the browser onto selected objects (MATERIALS/MATBROWSEROPEN opens the Materials Browser, MATEDITOROPEN the editor).
tools.usage:
MATERIALATTACH
(Material Attachment Options dialog: left list Drawing materials, right list Layers with current material; drag material onto layer; Detach button)
MATERIALMAP
Select an option [Box/Planar/Spherical/Cylindrical/copY mapping to/Reset mapping] <Box>:
Select faces or objects: <selection> Enter  (then adjust the mapping gizmo; Enter to accept)
MATERIALASSIGN  Select objects: ... (assigns the material currently selected in the browser)
CMATERIAL = material name applied to new objects (BYLAYER default)

parameters.name: Material ByLayer
parameters.description: Objects whose Material property is ByLayer follow the layer attachment; explicit materials override it.

parameters.name: MATERIALMAP Box / Planar / Spherical / Cylindrical
parameters.description: Projection type for texture coordinates; the gizmo moves, rotates and scales the map on the object.

parameters.name: copY mapping to
parameters.description: Apply the same mapping to other objects.

tools.example:
MATBROWSEROPEN (double-click 'Concrete - Cast-in-Place' and 'Glass - Clear' to load them into the drawing)
MATERIALATTACH
(drag Concrete onto layer A-WALL, Glass onto layer A-GLAZ; OK)
MATERIALMAP
B
(select the brick wall) Enter
(scale the gizmo so bricks are 215 mm) Enter
tools.notes: The Autodesk material library must be installed for the browser to show content; drawings carry the materials they use. Rendered materials show in the Realistic visual style when VSMATERIALMODE is 2 (materials and textures).

tools.name: POINTLIGHT
tools.description: Creates a point light (omnidirectional, like a bulb) at a location, with name, intensity, on/off status, photometric properties (candela, lumens, lux and lamp colour when LIGHTINGUNITS is photometric), shadows, attenuation and filter colour, or a target point light with the Target option. Lights are glyph objects that can be moved with grips, listed in LIGHTLIST and used by RENDER; they only have an effect when DEFAULTLIGHTING is 0.
tools.usage:
POINTLIGHT
Specify source location <0,0,0>: <point>
Enter an option to change [Name/Intensity factor/Status/Photometry/shadoW/Attenuation/filterColor/eXit] <eXit>:
Photometry: [Intensity/Color/eXit]  Intensity in candela (Cd), lux (Lx at distance) or lumens (Lm); Color as a colour temperature name (D65, Halogen, Fluorescent...) or Kelvin
shadoW: [Off/Sharp/soFt mapped/soft sAmpled]

parameters.name: Intensity factor
parameters.description: Multiplier on the photometric intensity (default 1).

parameters.name: Attenuation
parameters.description: Type None / Inverse Linear / Inverse Squared, with optional start/end limits (generic lighting only).

parameters.name: LIGHTINGUNITS
parameters.description: 0 generic (no photometry), 1 international (lux), 2 american (foot-candles) - photometric lighting is the default.

parameters.name: DEFAULTLIGHTING / DEFAULTLIGHTINGTYPE
parameters.description: 1 uses the automatic default lights and ignores user lights; 0 uses the lights in the model.

parameters.name: LIGHTGLYPHDISPLAY
parameters.description: 0 hides light glyphs in the viewport.

tools.example:
DEFAULTLIGHTING 0
POINTLIGHT
1500,1500,2700
N
CEILING-1
P
I
1200
X
W
F
X
tools.notes: Lights are stored in the drawing and can be placed on a layer that is frozen for plotting; freezing the layer also disables the light. Not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: SPOTLIGHT
tools.description: Creates a spotlight: a directional cone light with a source and a target point, a hotspot angle (full intensity) and a falloff angle (edge of the cone), plus the usual name, intensity, status, photometry, shadow, attenuation and filter colour options. Free spotlights (FREESPOT) have no target. Used to accent features in interior renderings and for stage/exhibition lighting studies.
tools.usage:
SPOTLIGHT
Specify source location <0,0,0>: <point>
Specify target location <0,0,-10>: <point>
Enter an option to change [Name/Intensity factor/Status/Photometry/Hotspot/Falloff/shadoW/Attenuation/filterColor/eXit] <eXit>:

parameters.name: Hotspot
parameters.description: Cone angle of full intensity, 0-160 degrees (default 45).

parameters.name: Falloff
parameters.description: Outer cone angle, must be >= hotspot (default 50); the difference gives the soft edge.

parameters.name: shadoW
parameters.description: Off / Sharp / soFt mapped (map size, softness) / soft sAmpled (shape, samples).

tools.notes: Grips on the glyph adjust hotspot and falloff interactively. Photometric webs (IES files) require WEBLIGHT instead.

tools.name: DISTANTLIGHT
tools.description: Creates a distant light - parallel rays from a direction, like the sun without its geographic calculation - defined by a from/to vector or a direction vector, with intensity, status, photometry, shadows and colour. WEBLIGHT creates a photometric web light whose distribution comes from an IES file (luminaire data from a manufacturer), the accurate choice for real fixtures. Both are listed and edited in LIGHTLIST.
tools.usage:
DISTANTLIGHT
Specify light direction FROM <0,0,0> or [Vector]: <point> | V
Specify light direction TO <1,1,1>: <point>
Enter an option to change [Name/Intensity factor/Status/Photometry/shadoW/filterColor/eXit] <eXit>:
WEBLIGHT
Specify source location <0,0,0>: <point>
Specify target location <0,0,-10>: <point>
Enter an option to change [Name/Intensity factor/Status/Photometry/weB/shadoW/filterColor/eXit]: weB > File: <path.ies>, X/Y/Z rotation

parameters.name: Vector
parameters.description: Give the light direction as a vector instead of two points.

parameters.name: weB > File
parameters.description: IES photometric data file; the glyph shows the distribution shape.

parameters.name: LIGHTINGUNITS
parameters.description: Distant lights with photometric units are discouraged (a warning appears); use SUNPROPERTIES for daylight.

tools.example:
DISTANTLIGHT
V
-1,-1,-2
N
FILL
I
0.4
X

WEBLIGHT 0,0,2700 0,0,0 W F C:/ies/downlight_15W.ies X X
tools.notes: Distant lights have no attenuation and no position. The sun (SUNPROPERTIES) is a special distant light driven by GEOGRAPHICLOCATION and date/time.

tools.name: LIGHTLIST
tools.description: Opens the Lights in Model palette listing every user-created light (point, spot, distant, web) by name and type, with on/off status; selecting a row selects the light in the drawing, and right-click offers Delete Light and Properties. The sun and sky are not listed here - they are managed in SUNPROPERTIES. LIGHTLISTCLOSE closes the palette; LIGHTLISTSTATE reports whether it is open.
tools.usage:
LIGHTLIST  (Visualize tab > Lights > dialog launcher)
LIGHTLISTCLOSE

parameters.name: Properties
parameters.description: Opens the Properties palette for the light: intensity, photometric values, shadows, attenuation, colour, position/target.

tools.example:
LIGHTLIST
(select CEILING-1 to CEILING-6 with Shift, right-click > Properties, set Lamp intensity 900 Cd)
tools.notes: Lights in xrefs are read-only here. Turning a light Off keeps it in the model without contributing to renders.

tools.name: SUNPROPERTIES
tools.description: Opens the Sun Properties palette controlling the sun light and sky: Status on/off (SUNSTATUS), intensity factor, colour, shadows, date and time (with daylight saving), azimuth/altitude (read-only, computed from GEOGRAPHICLOCATION), sky properties (Sky Off, Sky Background, Sky Background and Illumination; intensity factor, haze, horizon height/blur/ground colour, night colour, aerial perspective, visibility distance) and sun disk appearance. It drives daylight studies and exterior renderings. SUNPROPERTIESCLOSE closes it.
tools.usage:
SUNPROPERTIES  (Visualize tab > Sun & Location > dialog launcher)
SUNPROPERTIESCLOSE
System variables: SUNSTATUS 0|1, SKYSTATUS 0 off | 1 background | 2 background and illumination, LATITUDE, LONGITUDE, TIMEZONE, GEOLATLONGFORMAT

parameters.name: Date / Time
parameters.description: Set with the Sun & Location ribbon sliders or the palette; the sun position updates live in shaded views with shadows on (VSSHADOWS).

parameters.name: Sky Background and Illumination
parameters.description: Adds sky light and a gradient background to renders; requires photometric lighting units.

parameters.name: Rendered Shadow Details
parameters.description: Type Sharp / Soft, map size, softness.

tools.example:
GEOGRAPHICLOCATION (set the site)
SUNPROPERTIES
(Status On; Date 21 June; Time 15:00; Sky Background and Illumination; Intensity factor 1)
VSSHADOWS 2
RENDER
tools.notes: Shadows in viewports need hardware acceleration and a shaded visual style. The sun is ignored when DEFAULTLIGHTING is 1. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: VIEWBASE
tools.description: Creates a base drawing view (Model Documentation, 2013+) of the 3D solids and surfaces in model space, or of an Autodesk Inventor part/assembly/presentation file, on a layout: an associative 2D projection with hidden-line style, scale and visibility options, from which projected views (VIEWPROJ), section views (VIEWSECTION) and detail views (VIEWDETAIL) are derived. The views update when the model changes (VIEWUPDATE / VIEWUPDATEAUTO), replacing FLATSHOT/SOLVIEW workflows.
tools.usage:
VIEWBASE
Specify model source [Model space/File] <Model space>: M | F (browse for .ipt/.iam/.ipn)
Select objects or [Entire model] <Entire model>: <solids/surfaces> Enter
Enter new or existing layout name to place view or [?] <current>: <layout>
Specify location of base view or [Type/sElect/Orientation/Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility] <Type>: <point>
Select option [Select/Orientation/Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/Move/eXit] <eXit>:
(then) Specify location of projected view or <eXit>: (click positions for orthographic/isometric projections) Enter

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Base only, or Base and Projected (place several projections in one go).

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: Front, Top, Left, Right, Bottom, Back, and the four isometrics (SW/SE/NE/NW).

parameters.name: Hidden lines
parameters.description: Visible lines / Visible and hidden lines / Shaded with visible lines / Shaded with visible and hidden lines.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Absolute scale (1:2) or relative to the parent view.

parameters.name: Visibility
parameters.description: Interference edges, tangent edges (and shortening), bend extents, thread features, presentation trails.

parameters.name: VIEWUPDATEAUTO
parameters.description: 1 updates views automatically when the model changes; 0 requires VIEWUPDATE.

tools.example:
VIEWBASE
M

Sheet A3
(click the base position)
O
FRONT
S
1:2
X
(click above for Top, right for Right side, upper-right for isometric) Enter
tools.notes: Views are placed on the layout as drawing view objects with their own layers (MD_Visible, MD_Hidden, MD_Annotation... controlled by VIEWSTD); dimension them with DIM commands, which are associative to view edges. Works in the Core Console for batch view generation. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: VIEWPROJ
tools.description: Creates one or more projected views (orthographic or isometric) from an existing parent drawing view by dragging in the desired direction - vertical or horizontal drag gives the adjacent orthographic projection, diagonal gives an isometric. Projected views inherit the parent's scale, hidden-line style and visibility settings and stay aligned with it unless the alignment is broken.
tools.usage:
VIEWPROJ
Select parent view: <pick a drawing view>
Specify location of projected view or <eXit>: <point> (repeat) Enter
Select option [Undo/eXit] <eXit>:

parameters.name: projection angle
parameters.description: First-angle or third-angle placement follows the drafting standard set in VIEWSTD.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Projected views are constrained to the parent; right-click > Break Alignment to move freely.

tools.example:
VIEWPROJ
(pick the front view)
(click to the right, then above, then upper-right) Enter
tools.notes: Isometric projections use the parent's scale by default and can be re-scaled with VIEWEDIT. A view whose parent is deleted becomes a base view.

tools.name: VIEWSECTION
tools.description: Creates a section view from a parent drawing view by drawing the cutting line on it: Full (straight), Half, Offset (stepped), Aligned or Object (from an existing polyline/line). The result shows the cut faces hatched, the section line with identifier and arrows in the parent, a view label and optional depth (slice) control, all governed by the section view style (VIEWSECTIONSTYLE) and associative to the model.
tools.usage:
VIEWSECTION
Select parent view: <pick>
Hidden Lines = Visible lines, Scale = 1:2 (from parent)
Specify start point or [Type/Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/Projection/Depth/Annotation/hatCH] <Type>: <point>
Specify next point or [Undo]: <point> ... Enter (Done)
Specify location of section view or [Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/Projection/Depth/Annotation/hatCH/Move/eXit]: <point>
Type: [Full/Half/Offset/Aligned/Object]

parameters.name: Projection
parameters.description: Normal (perpendicular to the last segment) or Orthogonal placement.

parameters.name: Depth
parameters.description: Full, Slice (with a distance) or Custom - how far behind the cut plane geometry is shown.

parameters.name: Annotation
parameters.description: Identifier letter and whether the view label is shown.

parameters.name: hatCH
parameters.description: Toggle hatching of cut faces (pattern per material/style).

parameters.name: Section participation
parameters.description: Per-solid property (Section / None / Slice) in the parent view's component settings so fasteners can be excluded from cutting.

tools.example:
VIEWSECTION
(pick the plan view)
T
O
(click points for the stepped cut through both bores) Enter
(click below to place the section) X
tools.notes: Section lines can be constrained with VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH so they follow model edges. Views of Inventor models honour Inventor's section participation. The section view style controls hatch pattern, arrow style and label format.

tools.name: VIEWDETAIL
tools.description: Creates a detail view - an enlarged portion of a parent drawing view - by picking a centre and a circular or rectangular boundary; the detail is placed at a larger scale with a label and its boundary and identifier drawn in the parent, all styled by VIEWDETAILSTYLE. The model edge option controls whether the detail is shown with a smooth or jagged boundary edge and whether a connection line is drawn.
tools.usage:
VIEWDETAIL
Select parent view: <pick>
Specify center point or [Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/Boundary/model Edge/Annotation] <Boundary>: <point>
Specify size of boundary or [Rectangular/Circular/Undo]: <point/radius>
Specify location of detail view: <point>
Select option [Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/Boundary/model Edge/Annotation/Move/eXit] <eXit>:

parameters.name: Boundary
parameters.description: Circular or Rectangular detail boundary.

parameters.name: model Edge
parameters.description: Smooth, Smooth with border, Smooth with connection line, or Jagged.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Defaults to twice the parent scale; set explicitly (e.g. 2:1).

parameters.name: Annotation
parameters.description: Identifier letter and label visibility.

tools.example:
VIEWDETAIL
(pick the section view)
(click the centre of the O-ring groove)
15
(place the detail to the right)
S
5:1
X
tools.notes: Detail boundaries can be constrained to geometry with VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH. The detail label uses the style's label format with fields for identifier and scale.

tools.name: VIEWEDIT
tools.description: Edits an existing drawing view's hidden-line style, scale and visibility settings (and for section/detail views their specific options) from the command line, the same properties offered by the contextual Drawing View ribbon tab when a view is selected. VIEWUPDATE regenerates selected or all views after the source model changed when automatic updating is off, and VIEWCOMPONENT selects individual solids inside a view to change their section participation or hide them.
tools.usage:
VIEWEDIT
Select drawing view: <pick>
Select option [Hidden lines/Scale/Visibility/eXit] <eXit>:  (section views add Depth/Annotation/hatCH; detail views add Boundary/model Edge/Annotation)
VIEWUPDATE
Select drawing views to update or [All]: <selection> | A
VIEWCOMPONENT
Select component: <pick a solid in a view>  then set Section participation / Hide

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Changing the scale of a base view rescales its projected children.

parameters.name: VIEWUPDATEAUTO
parameters.description: 0 manual (views show an out-of-date badge until VIEWUPDATE), 1 automatic.

tools.example:
VIEWEDIT
(pick the base view)
H
V (visible and hidden lines)
S
1:5
X
VIEWUPDATE
A
tools.notes: Views out of date are marked with a red border/badge. Large models are faster with VIEWUPDATEAUTO 0 and a single VIEWUPDATE before plotting.

tools.name: VIEWSTD
tools.description: Opens the Drafting Standard dialog for Model Documentation: projection type (first angle or third angle), thread style (how threads are represented), shading/preview type and quality for shaded views, and the default section and detail view styles. It sets the drawing-wide conventions used by VIEWBASE and its derivatives and should be fixed in the template.
tools.usage:
VIEWSTD
(Drafting Standard dialog: Projection type [First angle/Third angle]; Thread style; Shading/Preview - preview type Shaded/Bounding box, shaded view quality; Section view style; Detail view style)

parameters.name: Projection type
parameters.description: First angle (ISO) or Third angle (ANSI) - determines where VIEWPROJ places projections.

parameters.name: Thread style
parameters.description: Options for representing threads from Inventor models.

parameters.name: Shaded view quality
parameters.description: DPI for shaded drawing views (higher = larger files).

tools.example:
VIEWSTD
(First angle; Section view style ISO; Detail view style ISO; OK)
tools.notes: Changing the projection type does not move existing views. The layers used by drawing views (MD_*) are created automatically and can be pre-defined in the template with the required colours and linetypes.

tools.name: VIEWSECTIONSTYLE
tools.description: Opens the Section View Style Manager to create and edit section view styles - Identifier and Arrows (identifier text style/height/position, arrow symbol, size, direction and extension), Cutting Plane (end/bend line style, show plane lines), View Label (text style, position, label pattern with fields for identifier and scale) and Hatch (pattern, angle, scale per material or fixed, transparency). VIEWDETAILSTYLE is the equivalent for detail views (identifier symbol, boundary line, model edge, view label). The current styles are chosen in VIEWSTD.
tools.usage:
VIEWSECTIONSTYLE
(Section View Style Manager: styles list, Set Current, New, Modify, Delete; tabs Identifier and Arrows / Cutting Plane / View Label / Hatch)
VIEWDETAILSTYLE
(Detail View Style Manager: Identifier / Detail Boundary / View Label tabs)

parameters.name: Label pattern
parameters.description: Text with fields, e.g. SECTION %<\AcVar ViewIdentifier>% - %<\AcVar ViewIdentifier>% ( %<\AcVar ViewScale>% ).

parameters.name: Hatch
parameters.description: Pattern from the .pat file, scale, angle alternating for adjacent parts, colour, transparency.

parameters.name: Arrow direction
parameters.description: Towards or away from the cutting plane, with extension and offset values.

tools.example:
VIEWSECTIONSTYLE
(New 'ISO-MECH' from Metric50; Hatch: ANSI31 scale 1.5; View Label: pattern 'SECTION %<\AcVar ViewIdentifier>%'; Set Current)
tools.notes: Styles are saved in the drawing and can be imported from another drawing with DesignCenter. Existing views keep their style; change it through the view's Properties.

tools.name: VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH
tools.description: Enters the symbol sketch mode for a section line or detail boundary so it can be constrained to the drawing view's geometry with geometric and dimensional constraints - e.g. a section line coincident with a hole centre, a detail circle concentric with a bore - keeping the symbol correctly placed when the model changes. VIEWSKETCHCLOSE exits the mode (VIEWSKETCHMODE reports it), and VIEWSETPROJ picks the Inventor project file used to resolve Inventor references.
tools.usage:
VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH
Select section line or detail boundary: <pick>
(apply GC*/DC* constraints between the symbol and view geometry; the Symbol Sketch ribbon tab shows Finish)
VIEWSKETCHCLOSE
VIEWSETPROJ  (Select Inventor project file dialog: .ipj)

parameters.name: constraints
parameters.description: Coincident, concentric, parallel, perpendicular, horizontal/vertical and dimensional constraints to view edges and centres.

parameters.name: VIEWSETPROJ
parameters.description: Needed when the Inventor assembly referenced by VIEWBASE uses a project (.ipj) to find its components.

tools.example:
VIEWSYMBOLSKETCH
(pick the section line)
GCCOINCIDENT (section line midpoint to the bore centre)
VIEWSKETCHCLOSE
tools.notes: Constraints in sketch mode are separate from model-space constraints. Unconstrained symbols simply stay where they were drawn when the view updates.

tools.name: 3DPRINT
tools.description: Prepares selected solids or watertight meshes for 3D printing: the 3D Print Options dialog shows the output bounding box dimensions, lets you scale the model to fit a printer and writes a binary STL file (FACETRES controls its smoothness), then hands over to Autodesk Print Studio if it is installed. 3DPRINTSERVICE (2017+) writes the STL and opens a web page of print service providers. STLOUT is the bare STL export without the dialog.
tools.usage:
3DPRINT
Select solids or watertight meshes: <selection> Enter
(3D Print Options dialog: Objects count, Output dimensions Length/Width/Height, Scale, Output preview; OK -> Create STL File dialog)
3DPRINTSERVICE  (same selection and dialog, then STL + browser)
STLOUT
Select solids or watertight meshes: <selection> Enter
Create a binary STL file? [Yes/No] <Y>:

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Uniform scale applied to the exported model (the drawing is unchanged).

parameters.name: FACETRES
parameters.description: Raise to 8-10 before export for smooth curved faces; STL is triangles only.

parameters.name: binary / ASCII STL
parameters.description: Binary is smaller; some slicers want ASCII.

parameters.name: units
parameters.description: STL has no units; 1 drawing unit = 1 STL unit, so model in mm or set INSUNITS accordingly for tools that read it.

tools.example:
FACETRES 10
STLOUT
(select the bracket) Enter
Y
C:/out/bracket.stl
tools.notes: Only closed solids and watertight meshes export; surfaces and open meshes are refused. Print Studio was discontinued; 3DPRINT now effectively produces the STL. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: 3DDWF
tools.description: Exports the 3D model space objects (or a selection) to a 3D DWF or DWFx file that Autodesk Design Review, Navisworks and the Autodesk Viewer can orbit, section and measure, optionally organised by xref/block hierarchy and including materials. 3DDWFPREC sets the tessellation precision. It is the lightweight 3D deliverable format that predates shared views.
tools.usage:
3DDWF
(Export 3D DWF dialog: file name .dwf/.dwfx; Options: Objects to export [All model space objects / Select model space objects], 3D DWF Organization [Group individual objects by xref hierarchy], Publish with materials)
Select objects or <all model space objects>:

parameters.name: 3DDWFPREC
parameters.description: 1 (coarse) to 6 (fine) tessellation of curved faces; default 2.

parameters.name: Group by xref hierarchy
parameters.description: Keeps the model tree navigable in the viewer.

parameters.name: Publish with materials
parameters.description: Embed material colours/textures.

tools.example:
3DDWFPREC 4
3DDWF
C:/issue/plant_3d.dwfx
(Options: all objects, group by xref, materials; OK)
tools.notes: 2D layouts are published with PUBLISH/EXPORTDWF; 3DDWF is model space only. SHAREVIEW (2019+) uploads a similar 3D representation to the Autodesk Viewer instead of a file.

tools.name: IMPORT
tools.description: Imports geometry from other CAD and exchange formats into the current drawing (or, for 3D formats, as a block/solids): 3D Studio (.3ds), ACIS (.sat), CATIA V4/V5 (.model, .CATPart, .CATProduct), FBX, IGES (.igs/.iges), JT, Windows Metafile (.wmf), MicroStation DGN, Siemens NX (.prt), Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b), Pro/ENGINEER and Creo (.prt/.asm/.g/.neu), Rhino (.3dm), SolidWorks (.prt/.sldprt/.asm/.sldasm), STEP (.ste/.stp/.step) and PDF (via PDFIMPORT). 3D CAD formats arrive as 3D solids and surfaces, translated in the background with a notification when done. IGESIMPORT / IGESEXPORT are dedicated commands for IGES.
tools.usage:
IMPORT
(Import File dialog: Files of type list; select the file; for CAD formats the translation runs in the background and reports 'Import complete' in the status bar)
-IMPORT: command-line prompts for the file name
IGESIMPORT  (Select IGES file)  /  IGESEXPORT  Select objects: ... (writes .igs/.iges)
EXPORT  (Files of type: 3D DWF, Metafile, ACIS, Lithography (STL), Encapsulated PS, DXX Extract, Bitmap, Block, V8 DGN, V7 DGN, IGES, FBX, ...)

parameters.name: 3D CAD formats
parameters.description: Solids come in as AutoCAD 3D solids (ShapeManager); assemblies become blocks per component; units are converted per INSUNITS.

parameters.name: Translation options
parameters.description: Some formats show an Options dialog (e.g. DGN mapping setup, FBX objects/lights/cameras/materials) before the import runs.

parameters.name: PDF
parameters.description: Handled by PDFIMPORT with its filters (vector geometry, fills, images, TrueType text).

parameters.name: STEP export
parameters.description: Available through EXPORT/Save As type STEP in recent releases via the Translator; there is no STEPOUT command.

tools.example:
IMPORT
(Files of type: STEP; choose housing.stp; OK)
(wait for 'Import complete', click the balloon to insert)

; IGES
IGESEXPORT
(select the solids) Enter
C:/out/housing.igs
tools.notes: The 3D translators are part of AutoCAD (not LT) since 2014 and run in a separate process; very large assemblies can take long and produce many blocks. Imported solids carry no parametric history; use VIEWBASE on them for drawings.

tools.name: REGEN3
tools.description: Regenerates all views in the drawing to repair display anomalies of 3D solids and surfaces (missing faces, wrong silhouettes, stale graphics cache) that a normal REGEN/REGENALL does not fix, by rebuilding the graphics for those objects from scratch (2017.1+). Run it when a model looks corrupt on screen but AUDIT reports no errors.
tools.usage: REGEN3  (no prompts)
tools.example:
; model displays holes in faces after a long editing session
REGEN3
tools.notes: Slower than REGEN because every 3D object is re-tessellated. It does not change the database, so no save is triggered.
